details: Minutes from the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) July meeting revealed that officials acknowledged inflation remained elevated. While the committee kept rates steady, several members favored an immediate hike, and many believed further tightening would likely be necessary if inflation fails to decline. This contrasts with current market expectations, which have lowered the probability of a September rate hike following subsequent softer economic data.
title: US Fed Minutes Show Lingering Inflation Concerns, Potential for More Hikes

details: Philip Lane, Chief Economist for the European Central Bank, indicated that Eurozone inflation is expected to remain around 3% for the rest of 2026. This persistence is attributed to elevated energy prices stemming from the US-Iran conflict. Lane emphasized that future ECB monetary policy decisions will be highly dependent on the conflict's evolution and inflation dynamics, with markets anticipating at least one more rate hike this year.
title: ECB Policymaker Warns Eurozone Inflation May Persist Due to Geopolitics

details: The U.S. Treasury Department announced plans to more than double its buyback operations for longer-term notes and bonds, starting in September. This move aims to stabilize the volatile bond market, leading to a notable pullback in government bond yields. Amid these developments, the cryptocurrency market rallied sharply, with Bitcoin surging approximately 6% to cross back above the $68,000 threshold, triggering a significant wave of short liquidations.
title: US Treasury Boosts Bond Buybacks, Bitcoin Jumps Above $68,000
